**Answer: the University of Bonn.** He began his medical studies there. Some sources say he also studied at other universities, so Bonn may not be the only one.

I ran the searches and page reads myself instead of spawning subagents, because the skill's file-writing workflow conflicts with your no-local-files rule. I used 3 of the 8 allowed retrievals, and one of them failed.

**Claims and sources**
- Aschoff (1913–1998) was a German physician and physiologist, regarded as a co-founder of chronobiology.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff
- After the Abitur he studied medicine at the University of Bonn.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff
- The LEO-BW biography says he began his medical studies in Bonn after finishing school in Freiburg in 1931. I only saw this through a search summary, because the page itself returned HTTP 403 when I tried to open it.
  https://www.leo-bw.de/en/detail/-/Detail/details/PERSON/kgl_biographien/104631406/Aschoff
- In 1938 he moved to the University of Göttingen to work on thermoregulation physiology with Hermann Rein. He later held a professorship there.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff

**Caveats**
- The search summary says LEO-BW has him continuing at the Freiburg medical faculty after Bonn. It says The Auk obituary has him moving through Göttingen, Würzburg and Heidelberg. I did not open either page, so I can't confirm the order or whether he finished his degree at a different university. The Auk obituary is here: https://bioone.org/journals/the-auk/volume-117/issue-3/0004-8038_2000_117_0779_IMJRA_2.0.CO_2/IN-MEMORIAM-J%C3%9CRGEN-ASCHOFF-19131998/10.1642/0004-8038(2000)117%5B0779:IMJRA%5D2.0.CO;2.full
- The sources I read give no years for his time at Bonn and don't say where he took his doctorate.
